before:
DateTimeImmutable does not mutate the original when modified. DateTimeZone supplies explicit zone rules. Fixed input instead of now makes the example reproducible.

The DateTimeImmutable constructor receives timestamp text and a DateTimeZone object and returns a new immutable date-time object. Because this timestamp text contains no zone of its own, the explicit UTC object supplies its interpretation; the constructor does not read the current time here.

setTimezone changes the local representation, not the instant. At 00:30 UTC on January 1, New York is still on December 31. format("Y-m-d") prints only the local date, not a complete global timestamp.

Expected output or behavior: 2025-01-01
2024-12-31. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why a date alone cannot identify a global instant. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A time zone changes the local clock and calendar used to show a moment.
This immutable date gives back a new value and keeps the original UTC value unchanged.
The output is `2025-01-01`, then `2024-12-31`. Half an hour after midnight in UTC is still the previous date in New York on this day.
Move the UTC time to lunchtime on the same day.
